name: Criminal Justice
description: Criminal justice programmes cover policing, corrections, courts and the law that governs them — investigation, criminal procedure, constitutional limits on searches and arrests, ethics and the use of force. In Florida the subject is taught two quite different ways: as a short certified ACADEMY that qualifies you to be sworn, and as an academic degree that does not.
degreesNote: 46 Florida public institutions and 6,939 credentials in the 2023 federal award year — one of the largest footprints in the state. ⚠⚠ But look at the split, because it is the whole decision: 3,677 of those were CERTIFICATES of under a year, which is the basic recruit academy, against 2,229 bachelor's degrees, 437 associate degrees and 335 master's. ⚠⚠⚠ The academy is what makes you eligible to be sworn as an officer; the degree is not, and no degree substitutes for it. Conversely the academy is not a degree and carries no college credit at some institutions. ⚠ So the honest framing is that these are two separate purchases that happen to share a subject: buy the academy to get hired, and buy the degree for promotion, federal agencies, or a move into administration, analysis or law. Corrections is a substantial part of this footprint in its own right, with its own shorter academy. ⚠ Note that private and corporate security (CIP 43.04, 15 Florida institutions and 533 credentials) recruits from the same students but is not counted here — that code is not yet in the site's CIP tree.

cips.note: Criminal justice and corrections — 46 Florida public institutions and 6,939 credentials in the 2023 federal award year. ⚠ Dominated by short certificates (3,677), which are the basic recruit academies, with 2,229 bachelor's degrees alongside. Criminal justice and police science alone runs at 34 institutions, corrections at 30.

Homeland security and related protective services — 11 Florida public institutions and 272 credentials, weighted to bachelor's and master's degrees. The analytic and federal end of this field rather than the patrol end.

related.note: ⚠ The other public-safety academy, taught at many of the same colleges and often in the same division. ⚠⚠ The pay comparison is worth making before you choose: Florida police officers have a median of $74,470 against firefighters' $58,550, but firefighting has the dual-certification route with paramedic that carries substantial hiring bonuses. Both are academy-first careers where the degree is for promotion.

⚠ A quieter alternative for someone drawn to the legal side of criminal justice rather than the enforcement side — and one worth knowing about, because criminal justice graduates frequently discover that the courtroom interested them more than the patrol car.
